findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed using a cell phone and then proceeded to don gloves and engage in food handling. Be sure to educate employees on when to wash hands when tasks are interrupted.  Discussed with PIC proper handwashing. Ensure to wash hands before donning gloves when tasks are interrupted, as this will help prevent contaminating food and/or food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There wasn’t any paper towels available at the handwashing in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC and paper towels were provided. Ensure that paper towels are available at every hand-sink to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There wasn’t a Certified Food Protection Manager present at the start of the inspection. Shortly afterwards, a CFPM arrived. PIC mentioned that the facility is in the process of getting two more employees certified. Ensure that there is at least 1 CFPM present during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: At the start of the inspection, there wasn’t a sanitizer bucket available for use. A sanitizer bucket was prepared to correct the violation. Ensure that sani buckets are always available during food preparation and service.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.comment:
3-403.11: Inspector observed chicken and refried beans on the hot holding table at 119F and 122F respectively. The food had been on the hot holding table for approximately one half hour according to the facility manager. The food was put into the microwave and reheated to 178F and 197F respectively for hot holding. The violation is considered corrected on site. Take care to follow proper reheating procedures for hot holding. Use thermometer to verify temperatures before putting the food on the hot holding table. 

(A) TCS FOOD cooked, cooled, and reheated shall be reheated to 165F for 15 seconds. (P) (B) If reheated with microwave, FOOD rotated, stirred, covered, and allowed to stand for 2 minutes covered. (P) (C) Commercially processed FOOD shall be reheated to 135F. (P) (D) Reheating may not exceed 2 hours.(P) (E) Unsliced portions of MEAT roasts may be reheated according to oven parameters and minimum TCS conditions. (C)

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the soda nozzles soiled. Maintain food contact surfaces properly cleaned and sanitized. The soda nozzles were put through dish and returned to the machine clean and sanitized.

3-304.11: (A) FOOD shall only contact surfaces of EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned. (B) SINGLE-SERVICE/USE ARTICLES (C) LINENS

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the soda nozzles on the lobby soda fountain to have mold accumulation. Wash, rinse and sanitize any time contaminations has occurred or at least once every 24hours. Soda nozzles were removed and put through dish. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces.

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

Chicken on the hot holding table reads 131F. Water in the table was low and the pan of chicken was short. Chicken had been on the table since noon. The chicken was discarded. New chicken is in the cooking process. Chicken is usually replaced with fresh at 4pm. The violation is considered corrected on site. Make sure to check the steam table to ensure that water has not evaporated, or leaked out at the drain.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a box of single use cups on the floor in the storage area. Take care to properly protect single use items at all times. Cups were moved up onto the shelf. Violation was corrected on site. 

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Lid for spices is cracked and repaired with a piece of tape. Replace the lid so that it is smooth and cleanable.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 
Observed soda residue in the hand sink. Use hand sinks for hand washing only. Dump drinks around corner in utility sink. Sink was cleaned at time of inspection.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C
Observed lid on refried beans cooling in the walk in to be tight on the container. The lid was popped in order to allow heat to escape the food more effectively.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following nonfood-contact areas to be in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. Entire deep fryer areas needs cleaned: baffles of the hood are heavily soiled (last cleaning date by C.F.B., Inc. was 12/2/21 - almost 1 year no cleaning service), metal walls have accumulation of grease debris, basket next to fryers on wall has grease and food build-up on grating, quesadilla maker has large accumulation of grease and food debris caked on the outside (particularly the back where the hinges are), and the floors behind the fryers/table/reach-in freezer have an build-up of food/grease/debris. Ensure the entire area is cleaned - wash, rinse, sanitize. Professionally service the hood system for a cleaning. Clean area before next routine inspection. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 5/3/22.
2. Interior fan of the reach-in cooler by the front hand sink has dust. Clean the fan.

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. Ensure staff has a cleaning schedule to prevent accumulations of debris/grease/food splash.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas to be no longer smooth and easily cleanable:
1. Multiple holes in the Nudo board/wall directly above the 3 compartment sink. Fill with caulk.
2. Ceiling the back between the prep area and the walk-in cooler/freezer has been re-constructed with bare wood. Seal the wood with paint and/or sealant. Caulk the sides of the wood so there are no holes between the wall and wooden ceiling.
3. Holes present above the mop area on the wall - caulk to fill.

Ensure repairs before next routine inspection. #1 and partially #2 are repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 5/3/22. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed employee to improperly wash hands - no barrier was used to turn off the faucet handles. Ensure a barrier such as a paper towel is utilized to turn off the handles after properly washing hands - warm water and lather with soap for 20 seconds. Discussed with employee and PIC. COS.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed the reach-in cooler along the prep line to be holding at ~53-57 degrees F. All items prepped within the last several hours were brought to the walk-in cooler. Items voluntarily discarded included: sour cream individual package (box), chocolate milk, large container of coleslaw, thawed corn dogs. Sour cream was probed at 55 degrees F. Reach-in cooler has either failed and/or needs serviced. Cooler was turned up in the mean time before service call tomorrow (already scheduled). Cooler should not be used for foods that must be below 41 degrees F. Discussed with all employee’s and PIC. Keep refrigerated foods in the walk-in cooler until the reach-in cooler is fixed. Provided temperature log for facility to maintain morning and nightly temperature checks of both reach-in cooler and walk-in cooler. Inspector will follow-up on 5/5/22.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Observed multiple in-use rags to be on the counters of the prep table in the back kitchen. Discussed practices with employees. In-use rags should be maintained in sanitizer solution bucket with appropriate concentration of sanitizer when not utilized. Rags should not be stored on counter tops. COS.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed all food handler’s cards to be expired. Ensure folder with certification papers to be updated. Food handler’s cards are good for 3 years. Ensure new hires have food handler’s certification within 30 days of employment and copies are kept in the public health folder. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

(REPEAT) Observed all allergen training certification completed by the CFPM’s to be expired. Provided informational page on re-taking training. Certification is valid for 3 years. Ensure all food manager’s re-take the allergen training course and copies of the certification are left at the facility. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/20/22.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Corn dog on middle shelf of reach in cooler probed at internal temperature of 48F. Probe thermometer placed between bags of sour cream on bottom shelf of reach in cooler read 55F. Tamales on top shelf of this reach in cooler probed at 41F. It appears as though the unit is not cooling the bottom shelves appropriately. Corn dogs were discarded--these items had been in the cooler all day. Employee states temperature in this cooler was 45F this morning and that was the last time they took a temperature. Cold holding units must maintain cold TCS foods at internal temperatures of 41F or below at all times. Have unit serviced to maintain foods at 41F or below. DO not use middle/bottom shelves until it can maintain foods at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: As per routine inspection. This is scheduled to be cleaned and replaced at 6 month intervals by CFD, who was last here in December 2018.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment: Observed refried beans that had been cooked yesterday, reported to have been placed in the walk in freezer for 2 hours to cool, and then transferred to the walk in cooler to be probed with a recently calibrated digital stem thermometer at 50F at the time of the inspection (almost 24 hours later). Beans are in a large multi-gallon container with the lid sealed tightly. Refried beans were discarded at the time of the inspection and cooling was discussed.  3-501.14  (P)  Food did not cool from 135°F to 70°F within two hours and from 135°F to 41°F or less within a total of 6 hours. Reviewed cooling requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately cooled food was discarded. Reference 3-501.14.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: As above, the refried beans were in a large plastic multi-gallon container with the lid on tight in the walk in cooler. When cooling, especially with dense foods such as refried beans, large quantities must be divided into smaller portions in shallow pans for rapid cooling. 3-501.15  (Pf) Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment: Facility has an infrared thermometer, but no stem (probe) thermometer is able to be located at the time of the inspection. A thermometer for taking internal temperatures of food must be provided and used. Infrared thermometers only take a surface temperature of foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12  (Pf) A food thermometer is not available. Food thermometers shall be provided and readily accessible to ensure proper food temperatures. Reference 4-302.12.
